text: I would trade the last cookie for a whole bowl of popcorn.

text: I save the chocolate part of a cookie until my popcorn is gone.

text: I like a snack plate that has exactly as much fruit as cookies.

text: I prefer a warm cookie to ice cream even on a sunny day.

text: I take fruit on a journey and buy a pretzel on the way anyway.

text: I would build a cookie bridge over a bowl of ice cream.

text: I can hear popcorn being opened from farther away than my own name.

text: I would swap my fancy bento for a friend's enormous pretzel.

text: I think fruit tastes better when someone else has arranged it nicely.

text: I like pretzel crunch in my ice cream more than another scoop.

text: I pick a bento for its tiny compartments before checking the food.

text: I would carry a cookie in a special box so it stays unbroken.

text: I need a salty pretzel after sweet fruit to feel finished snacking.

text: I would make a popcorn necklace just to keep my snack nearby.

text: I offer a bite of ice cream even when it is my favourite flavour.

text: I would choose a picnic with great snacks over a picnic with a great view.

text: I break cookies over popcorn so every handful gets a surprise.

text: I think a fruit bowl should include at least one ridiculous tiny fork.

text: I would eat a pretzel in little loops before touching the middle.

text: I enjoy arranging snacks almost as much as eating them.

text: I would wait for ice cream instead of accepting a perfectly good cookie now.

text: I put the best fruit at the bottom of the bowl to reward my future self.

text: I would take a bento to a movie if everyone promised not to stare.

text: I would share a giant pretzel with someone who bites the wrong side.

text: I let ice cream soften while I carefully choose a topping.

text: I would add a pretzel to a balanced lunch purely because it fits.

text: I save fruit stickers longer than I save the fruit.

text: I would let a friend choose my snack if I could choose theirs.

text: I think popcorn belongs in a bowl large enough to need both hands.

text: I would mix fruit into ice cream even if it spoils the perfect swirl.

text: I would rather split two different snacks than have one all to myself.

text: I gather popcorn into one last handful instead of making several tiny trips.

text: I would take cookies as a thank-you gift and hope one comes back to me.

text: I think a pretzel needs company even when I said I wanted a small snack.

text: I would make a tiny fruit picnic for someone having a dull afternoon.

text: I rotate a cookie while eating so the last bite has the best edge.

text: I prefer snacks that can be eaten while holding a very important imaginary trophy.
